body.title: [Tests][Wasm] Add grouping Wasm codegen/box and compatibility testrunners
body.body:
Introduce grouping of Wasm tests and migrate there several testrunners for
- codegen/box tests and
- Klib forward compatibility testing. 

Goal: optimize CI time by avoiding lots of per-test overhead mainly from deserialization/lowering/generating of stdlib.
Statisics of local run on Macbook M4: 
- old FirWasmJsCodegenBoxTestGenerated: 25.5 mins
- new grouped WasmJsCodegenBoxTestGenerated: 16 mins

Similar proportion holds for dozen of other migrated testrunners in this PR.
With this improvement, a possibility to move Klib compatibility tests to Aggregate will be unlocked

Unfortunately, I cannot show the CI improvement on real builds, due to interference with TeamCity's misfeature about parallel build for Wasm codegen testing (https://www.jetbrains.com/help/teamcity/parallel-tests.html). After merge to master, the second Aggregate build will be much shorter.

Codegen and forward compatibility tests share a grouping logic, so it's cleaner to introduce them at the same time to see where the logic is the same, and where the specifics differ.
There exist more codegen/box-related testrunners, but they should be better migrated in scope of next PRs.
Caveat: So far no execution path is invented for grouping of multi-module tests(AbstractWasmJsCodegenMultiModuleTest, AbstractWasmJsCodegenCoroutinesStackSwitchingMultiModuleTest), so that tests are forced to be isolated, and that testrunners execution stays the same as their removed non-grouped testrunners.

Deep Review of the Last Commit 99487d8c — "Tests Add grouping Wasm codegen/box and compatibility testrunners"
This is the rebased/squashed version of the Wasm grouping commit 69 files, +3031/−580 and now incorporates all the refactors from our prior sessions. Notably, every critical bug flagged in earlier reviews is now fixed in the committed code. The remaining items are minor design/style nits.

Scope:
Introduces the two‑stage grouping test infrastructure for WASM codegen/box tests and the custom second‑stage klib‑compatibility runner. Wires new facades/runners, adds an isolator, and adjusts
generators/configuration to drive grouped execution.

What changed by area
• Test infra core
 • AbstractWasmSecondStageGroupingFacade.kt: New abstraction that builds/links grouped batches launcher generation, dependency aggregation, batch settings, helpers.
 • WasmFirstStageFacade.kt: Extracts common Stage‑1 helpers used by multiple facades.
 • WasmInProcessSecondStageFacade.kt(for codegen tests), CustomWasmJsCompilerSecondStageFacade.kt(for compatibility tests): Adapted to call the new base and route batches appropriately.
 • WasmCompilationSetsBoxRunnerGroupingStage.kt, WasmBoxRunnerBase.kt, WasmBoxRunner.kt, WasiBoxRunner.kt: Runner side to execute grouped batches across JS/WASI; save artifacts, run VMs, parse outcomes.
 • WasmGroupingTestIsolator.kt: Decides which tests must be isolated vs batched, and adds batch tokens e.g., for EH modes.
• Generation & wiring
 •   GenerateWasmTests.kt: Generates the grouped suites to use the new base/handlers.
 •   Gradle wiring: wasm/wasm.tests/build.gradle.kts, klib‑compat counterpart, and repo/.../jsTest.kt: Hooked the grouped engine into tasks requires enableGroupingTestEngine = true at the project layer; this commit appears to include that wiring for WASM suites.
• Companion adjustments
 • AbstractLauncherAdditionalSourceProvider.kt, batch insertion BatchingPackageInserter.kt, suppressors CustomKlibCompilerSecondStageTestSuppressor.kt, and other glue pieces to ensure launchers/directives interact correctly with grouped flow.

What's Done Well
• Documentation remains exemplary. The KDoc on WasmJsLauncherAdditionalSourceProvider explaining why per-test launcher classes must be baked into the Stage-1 KLIB because isolatedWithBox runs only WasmConfigurationPhase + WasmBackendPipelinePhase, so free-arg sources are ignored is the kind of comment that prevents real future regressions. Same for the BatchExecutionContext invariants and the isSingleTestBatch vs isIsolatedBatch dispatch rationale.
• Real strategy extraction. BatchExecutionContext + buildBatchExecutionContext(...) centralize the repeated pre-path computation settings aggregation, helper-KLIB dedup, dependency cleaning and are consumed by both facades.
The in-process isolatedWithBox/isolatedWithoutBox merge into doIsolatedInProcess(hasBox) is correct.
• JS companion collision detection. copyJsFilesToOutputDir now fails fast via testInfraError when two modules supply same-named .js/.mjs with different content, instead of silently last-write-wins.
• TestServices mutation tightly scoped. withTemporarySingleModuleStructure(...) replaces the inline register/restore, with a good rationale comment.
• Malformed-group validation. The new checkTestInfrastructure(...) loop in the CLI runner asserting all tests in a group share the same EH directive is a sensible guardrail with actionable messages.
• error(...) → testInfraError(...) for the "Unknown mode: $mode" branch — better infra-failure messaging.

Remaining Minor Issues / Questionable Decisions
1. copyJsFilesToOutputDir still rewrites identical duplicates. Collision detection is correct, but on a duplicate filename with identical content it still calls writeText again each time. A small else-skip after tracking
would avoid redundant I/O and make intent clearer.
2. BatchExecutionContext is eagerly built even on the isolated path. WasmInProcessSecondStageFacade.transform builds the full context up front, then the isolated branch uses only a subset. Acceptable not hot, but the "minimal path" is less explicit than it could be.
3. Cache lifecycle. GroupingTestIsolator.sourceContainsCache is now a ConcurrentHashMap good for contention, but keys TestModuleStructure are strongly retained for the classloader lifetime — minor unbounded-growth risk in long multi-suite runs. Acceptable for test infra; worth a lifecycle hook if memory ever becomes an issue.

Verdict
• The commit is a strong foundational step: it introduces a reusable grouping base for Stage‑2, proper runners, and initial isolation logic, while integrating with generation and Gradle wiring.
• Commit quality: strong. The two-stage grouping architecture is coherent, the documentation is top-tier, and all previously-identified correctness bugs are resolved in this revision.

Next steps: 
- migrate klib backward compatibility tests
- try to migrate remaining codegen-related tests

pullRequests.title: [Tests][Wasm] Add grouping Wasm codegen/box and compatibility testrunners
pullRequests.body:
Introduce grouping of Wasm tests and migrate there several testrunners for
- codegen/box tests and
- Klib forward compatibility testing. 

Goal: optimize CI time by avoiding lots of per-test overhead mainly from deserialization/lowering/generating of stdlib.
Statisics of local run on Macbook M4: 
- old FirWasmJsCodegenBoxTestGenerated: 25.5 mins
- new grouped WasmJsCodegenBoxTestGenerated: 16 mins

Similar proportion holds for dozen of other migrated testrunners in this PR.
With this improvement, a possibility to move Klib compatibility tests to Aggregate will be unlocked

Unfortunately, I cannot show the CI improvement on real builds, due to interference with TeamCity's misfeature about parallel build for Wasm codegen testing (https://www.jetbrains.com/help/teamcity/parallel-tests.html). After merge to master, the second Aggregate build will be much shorter.

Codegen and forward compatibility tests share a grouping logic, so it's cleaner to introduce them at the same time to see where the logic is the same, and where the specifics differ.
There exist more codegen/box-related testrunners, but they should be better migrated in scope of next PRs.
Caveat: So far no execution path is invented for grouping of multi-module tests(AbstractWasmJsCodegenMultiModuleTest, AbstractWasmJsCodegenCoroutinesStackSwitchingMultiModuleTest), so that tests are forced to be isolated, and that testrunners execution stays the same as their removed non-grouped testrunners.

Deep Review of the Last Commit 99487d8c — "Tests Add grouping Wasm codegen/box and compatibility testrunners"
This is the rebased/squashed version of the Wasm grouping commit 69 files, +3031/−580 and now incorporates all the refactors from our prior sessions. Notably, every critical bug flagged in earlier reviews is now fixed in the committed code. The remaining items are minor design/style nits.

Scope:
Introduces the two‑stage grouping test infrastructure for WASM codegen/box tests and the custom second‑stage klib‑compatibility runner. Wires new facades/runners, adds an isolator, and adjusts
generators/configuration to drive grouped execution.

What changed by area
• Test infra core
 • AbstractWasmSecondStageGroupingFacade.kt: New abstraction that builds/links grouped batches launcher generation, dependency aggregation, batch settings, helpers.
 • WasmFirstStageFacade.kt: Extracts common Stage‑1 helpers used by multiple facades.
 • WasmInProcessSecondStageFacade.kt(for codegen tests), CustomWasmJsCompilerSecondStageFacade.kt(for compatibility tests): Adapted to call the new base and route batches appropriately.
 • WasmCompilationSetsBoxRunnerGroupingStage.kt, WasmBoxRunnerBase.kt, WasmBoxRunner.kt, WasiBoxRunner.kt: Runner side to execute grouped batches across JS/WASI; save artifacts, run VMs, parse outcomes.
 • WasmGroupingTestIsolator.kt: Decides which tests must be isolated vs batched, and adds batch tokens e.g., for EH modes.
• Generation & wiring
 •   GenerateWasmTests.kt: Generates the grouped suites to use the new base/handlers.
 •   Gradle wiring: wasm/wasm.tests/build.gradle.kts, klib‑compat counterpart, and repo/.../jsTest.kt: Hooked the grouped engine into tasks requires enableGroupingTestEngine = true at the project layer; this commit appears to include that wiring for WASM suites.
• Companion adjustments
 • AbstractLauncherAdditionalSourceProvider.kt, batch insertion BatchingPackageInserter.kt, suppressors CustomKlibCompilerSecondStageTestSuppressor.kt, and other glue pieces to ensure launchers/directives interact correctly with grouped flow.

What's Done Well
• Documentation remains exemplary. The KDoc on WasmJsLauncherAdditionalSourceProvider explaining why per-test launcher classes must be baked into the Stage-1 KLIB because isolatedWithBox runs only WasmConfigurationPhase + WasmBackendPipelinePhase, so free-arg sources are ignored is the kind of comment that prevents real future regressions. Same for the BatchExecutionContext invariants and the isSingleTestBatch vs isIsolatedBatch dispatch rationale.
• Real strategy extraction. BatchExecutionContext + buildBatchExecutionContext(...) centralize the repeated pre-path computation settings aggregation, helper-KLIB dedup, dependency cleaning and are consumed by both facades.
The in-process isolatedWithBox/isolatedWithoutBox merge into doIsolatedInProcess(hasBox) is correct.
• JS companion collision detection. copyJsFilesToOutputDir now fails fast via testInfraError when two modules supply same-named .js/.mjs with different content, instead of silently last-write-wins.
• TestServices mutation tightly scoped. withTemporarySingleModuleStructure(...) replaces the inline register/restore, with a good rationale comment.
• Malformed-group validation. The new checkTestInfrastructure(...) loop in the CLI runner asserting all tests in a group share the same EH directive is a sensible guardrail with actionable messages.
• error(...) → testInfraError(...) for the "Unknown mode: $mode" branch — better infra-failure messaging.

Remaining Minor Issues / Questionable Decisions
1. copyJsFilesToOutputDir still rewrites identical duplicates. Collision detection is correct, but on a duplicate filename with identical content it still calls writeText again each time. A small else-skip after tracking
would avoid redundant I/O and make intent clearer.
2. BatchExecutionContext is eagerly built even on the isolated path. WasmInProcessSecondStageFacade.transform builds the full context up front, then the isolated branch uses only a subset. Acceptable not hot, but the "minimal path" is less explicit than it could be.
3. Cache lifecycle. GroupingTestIsolator.sourceContainsCache is now a ConcurrentHashMap good for contention, but keys TestModuleStructure are strongly retained for the classloader lifetime — minor unbounded-growth risk in long multi-suite runs. Acceptable for test infra; worth a lifecycle hook if memory ever becomes an issue.

Verdict
• The commit is a strong foundational step: it introduces a reusable grouping base for Stage‑2, proper runners, and initial isolation logic, while integrating with generation and Gradle wiring.
• Commit quality: strong. The two-stage grouping architecture is coherent, the documentation is top-tier, and all previously-identified correctness bugs are resolved in this revision.

Next steps: 
- migrate klib backward compatibility tests
- try to migrate remaining codegen-related tests

messages.author: jmrtsh
messages.body:
My worry is the DevEx overall with this change. I think we will have more WTF moments whether we go with heuristics or with explicit directives. But with directives, everyone has to learn one new thing, and that's it, WTF moments don't really happen anymore once everyone gets this. In addition, for me personally, I usually start from an existing similar test when I add a new one. So I'd see the new directive in existing tests first, before I run into a WTF moment. Won't prevent all of them of course. 

With heuristics, people will undoubtedly run into situations where they break down, and that's going to be way harder to debug. Not to mention maintaining these will be annoying, but thats the case for the directives as well. 

But precisely because of the increase in overall WTF moments, in either case, I'm not sure about the whole change. What's the gain in CI time for this? After all, developer time is a lot more expensive than CI time per minute. So if it saves 50% of a 2 hour CI run, it might be worth it, if it's 5 minutes, I'm not sure the additional developer time spent, both for using this infra, and maintaining 2.5k additional lines, is worth it.
